The table: versions, metadata, schema, protocol

Source: R/table.R
lake_versions.Rd

Functions that describe the table a snapshot holds, each from the log alone; none reads a data file.

Usage

lake_versions(tbl)

lake_history(tbl, limit = NULL, int64 = c("double", "integer64"))

lake_metadata(tbl)

lake_schema(tbl)

lake_partition_columns(tbl)

lake_properties(tbl)

lake_protocol(tbl)

lake_summary(tbl, int64 = c("double", "integer64"))

Arguments

tbl

A snapshot, from lake_open().

limit

The number of commits to return, newest first. NULL, the default, returns all of them.

int64

How 64-bit integers from the log are returned: "double" (the default), exact up to 2^53 - 1 and an error of class zulake_error_int64 beyond it, or "integer64", from the bit64 package, exact from -2^63 + 1 to 2^63 - 1 (bit64 keeps -2^63 for NA, so that value is an error too). It applies to the columns that hold 64-bit counts and values; inside an action or commitInfo as the log writes it, only a number a double cannot hold becomes an integer64.

Value

lake_versions(): a data frame version, timestamp (POSIXct, UTC), oldest first.

lake_history(): a data frame version, timestamp (the commit time), operation and commit_info, a list column holding each commit's commitInfo action as the log writes it (NULL for a commit without one), newest first.

lake_metadata(): a data frame of one row: id, name, description, format_provider, format_options (a list column), created_time (POSIXct, or NA), partition_columns (a list column) and configuration (a list column; see also lake_properties()).

lake_schema(): a data frame name, type (the Delta type, such as "long", "decimal(10,2)" or "timestamp_ntz", which is the zone-less timestamp; "struct", "array" or "map" for a nested column), nullable, partition (whether it is a partition column), physical_name (its name in the data files under column mapping, NA otherwise), metadata and type_detail (list columns: the column's metadata, and the nested type as the log writes it, NULL for a primitive one).

lake_partition_columns(): a character vector.

lake_properties(): a data frame key, value and default (TRUE for a property the table does not set, filled in with the protocol's default), sorted by key.

lake_protocol(): a data frame with one row per requirement: first readerVersion and writerVersion with their version, then each feature, with reader and writer saying which list of the protocol names it, and supported, whether zulake reads a table that needs it. Writer requirements are always supported: zulake does not write. A snapshot only exists for a table zulake can read, so every row of a snapshot's protocol is supported; the zulake_error_unsupported_feature error of a table that is refused carries the same data frame in its protocol field.

lake_summary(): a data frame of one row: version, timestamp, files, bytes, records (as lake_count() counts them, NA when a file has no numRecords), deleted_rows (the cardinality of the deletion vectors), files_with_deletion_vectors and files_without_records.

Details

  • lake_versions(): every version up to the snapshot's whose commit is still in the log, with its commit time.

  • lake_history(): the commitInfo of those commits, newest first.

  • lake_metadata(): the table's metaData action, in one row.

  • lake_schema(): one row per top-level column.

  • lake_partition_columns(): the partition columns, in order.

  • lake_properties(): the table's configuration, with the defaults the protocol states filled in.

  • lake_protocol(): the reader and writer versions and every feature, each marked supported or not.

  • lake_summary(): one row of totals.

The commit time of a version is the commit's in-commit timestamp when the table records them, and the commit file's modification time otherwise, as the protocol prescribes and as lake_open(timestamp =) uses it.

See also

lake_files() for the files, lake_actions() for a commit's actions.

Examples

path <- tempfile("table")
dir.create(file.path(path, "_delta_log"), recursive = TRUE)
writeLines(c(
  '{"commitInfo":{"timestamp":1767225600000,"operation":"CREATE TABLE"}}',
  '{"protocol":{"minReaderVersion":1,"minWriterVersion":2}}',
  paste0(
    '{"metaData":{"id":"example","name":"orders","format":{"provider":"parquet","options":{}},',
    '"schemaString":"{\\"type\\":\\"struct\\",\\"fields\\":[{\\"name\\":',
    '\\"id\\",\\"type\\":\\"long\\",\\"nullable\\":true,\\"metadata\\":{}}]}",',
    '"partitionColumns":[],"configuration":{"delta.appendOnly":"true"}}}'
  ),
  paste0(
    '{"add":{"path":"part-0.parquet","partitionValues":{},"size":100,',
    '"modificationTime":0,"dataChange":true,"stats":"{\\"numRecords\\":3}"}}'
  )
), file.path(path, "_delta_log", "00000000000000000000.json"))

tbl <- lake_open(path)
lake_versions(tbl)
#>   version           timestamp
#> 1       0 2026-11-26 15:34:20
lake_history(tbl)[c("version", "operation")]
#>   version    operation
#> 1       0 CREATE TABLE
lake_metadata(tbl)[c("id", "name")]
#>        id   name
#> 1 example orders
lake_schema(tbl)[c("name", "type", "nullable")]
#>   name type nullable
#> 1   id long     TRUE
lake_partition_columns(tbl)
#> character(0)
lake_properties(tbl)
#>                                   key value default
#> 1                    delta.appendOnly  true   FALSE
#> 2   delta.checkpoint.writeStatsAsJson  true    TRUE
#> 3 delta.checkpoint.writeStatsAsStruct false    TRUE
#> 4            delta.columnMapping.mode  none    TRUE
#> 5        delta.enableVariantShredding false    TRUE
#> 6     delta.parquet.compression.codec  zstd    TRUE
#> 7        delta.parquet.format.version 1.0.0    TRUE
#> 8          delta.rowTrackingSuspended false    TRUE
lake_protocol(tbl)
#>            name reader writer version supported
#> 1 readerVersion   TRUE  FALSE       1      TRUE
#> 2 writerVersion  FALSE   TRUE       2      TRUE
lake_summary(tbl)
#>   version           timestamp files bytes records deleted_rows
#> 1       0 2026-11-26 15:34:20     1   100       3            0
#>   files_with_deletion_vectors files_without_records
#> 1                           0                     0

unlink(path, recursive = TRUE)
